p: Article 44 (a Directive Principle) says the State shall try to secure a UCC for the whole country. Gujarat became the second State, after Uttarakhand, to pass a UCC Bill.

Courts have pushed it again and again: Shah Bano (1985) asked Parliament to frame a law; Sarla Mudgal (1995) stressed gender equality; John Vallamattom (2003) linked it to national integration; Jose Paulo Coutinho (2019) cited Goa's civil code as a working model; Shayara Bano (2017) struck down instant triple talaq.
Goa already follows a common civil code that dates to the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.
The 21st Law Commission said a UCC was neither necessary nor desirable at that stage.
Today communities follow separate personal laws (Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1936, and so on); the Special Marriage Act 1954 offers a civil-law marriage outside religion.
FSSAI licences and registrations now have perpetual validity, so there are no periodic renewals.
Registration alone is enough for turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore (raised from Rs 12 lakh); a State licence applies from Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 50 crore; a Central licence applies above Rs 50 crore.

FSSAI is a statutory body under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, which replaced eight earlier laws and orders including the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954. It sits under the Health Ministry and runs Eat Right India and front-of-pack labelling work.
Street vendors registered under the Street Vendors Act 2014 are treated as registered with FSSAI. Imported food must have at least 60% of shelf life (or three months) left at clearance.
A Parliamentary Committee found only 2% of inspections reported non-compliance, and noted just 266 labs, many unable to test heavy metals, pesticides or bacteria.

topics.t: CAPF Bill 2026 and Consumer Justice Report
p: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill covers CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB; Assam Rifles and NSG are not included at present.
It fixes deputation of IPS officers: 50% of IG posts, at least 67% of Additional DG posts and all Director General and Special DG posts.
Consumer Justice Report 2026 (India Justice Report): case pendency rose 21% between 2020 and 2024; the share of cases resolved fell from about 35% (2021) to 29% (2025).
Only 134 cases were sent to mediation across 23 States, and nearly half of State Commissions had no sitting president.
Postal voting is governed by the Conduct of Election Rules 1961 and the Representation of the People Act 1951.

It now also reaches electors above 85 and persons with disabilities. Service voters (armed forces, central police forces) and absentee voters (such as those in preventive detention) are covered; the President and Governors count among special voters.
The Media Certification and Monitoring Committee (MCMC) checks that political ads follow Election Commission rules and watches for suspected paid news.
Sujal Gaon ID is a digital ID for village piped water schemes under Jal Jeevan Mission, linked to the Sujalam Bharat digital system, supporting Har Ghar Jal by 2028.

topics.t: US-Iran war and its effects on India
p: The US and Israel launched coordinated strikes ('Operation Epic Fury') that killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei; Iran hit US bases, Israel and Gulf energy and civilian sites.

Brent crude crossed 110 dollars after strikes on Kharg Island and South Pars; Hormuz closure caused port congestion; Middle East shipping insurance rose 50%; rising costs could push 8.8 million people in 14 countries into poverty.

India's exposure: about half of its crude imports, 80-85% of LPG imports and about 60% of LNG imports pass the Strait of Hormuz; each 1 dollar rise in oil adds 1.8-2 billion dollars to the import bill; about 10 million Indians live in the Gulf; IMEC was paralysed.

Response: seven inter-ministerial empowered groups as rapid-response teams, a proposed Rs 573 billion stabilisation fund, direct PM outreach across West Asia, and wider fertiliser sourcing (Russia, Morocco, Australia, Canada, Indonesia, Egypt).

topics.t: Strategic locations affected by the conflict
p: Strait of Hormuz: between Iran and Oman, linking the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman. About 15 million barrels a day (about 34% of global crude trade) pass through; about a fifth of world liquid petroleum and LNG trade.

Fujairah (UAE) lies outside the Strait on the Gulf of Oman, letting the UAE bypass it. Kharg Island exports about 90% of Iranian crude. South Pars is the world's largest gas field, shared by Iran and Qatar.
Al Udeid (Qatar) is the largest US base in the region; the US Fifth Fleet is at Juffair, Manama (Bahrain). Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan are Iranian nuclear sites.
The Red Sea reaches the Gulf of Aden via Bab-el-Mandeb and the Mediterranean via Suez, carrying about 12% of world trade.

topics.t: Energy security and India's foreign policy
p: India imports over 85% of its crude and about 50% of its gas; crude suppliers grew from 27 countries (2006-07) to about 40.
Energy use is expected to rise from about 775 Mtoe (2013) to about 1,250 Mtoe (2030).

Steps: Strategic Petroleum Reserves phase II (Chandikhol in Odisha, Padur in Karnataka); HPCL's 10-year LNG deal with UAE's ADNOC; PSUs hold 48 assets in 22 countries; the Mercantile Marine Domain Awareness Centre watches chokepoints.
India also leads the Global Biofuel Alliance (with G20) and the International Solar Alliance.

Tension rests on the Durand Line (about 2,600 km, drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan). Pakistan treats it as its border; Afghanistan sees an imposed colonial line and raises Pashtun nationalism.
Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan emerged in 2007. In the latest round Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab Lil-Haq and Afghanistan launched Radd al-Zulm.
Qatar and Turkey brokered only a temporary peace; Saudi-mediated talks collapsed toward the end of 2025. India condemned Pakistan's air strikes.
India sees its Afghan work (Salma 'Afghan-India Friendship' Dam) as humanitarian and development; it could revive the air freight corridor and Chabahar.
Both sides signed Terms of Reference for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement to take trade to 50 billion dollars by 2030 (it was about 8.66 billion in 2024-25).

Cameco uranium deal of about 2.6 billion dollars for 2027-2035 under the 2010 Civil Nuclear Cooperation Agreement; imported-uranium reactors stay under IAEA safeguards. India imports about 70% of its uranium; its ore is only 0.02-0.45% grade against Canada's 10-100 times richer ore; target is 100 GW nuclear by 2047.
Canada will join the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance; India backs Canada as an IORA dialogue partner; a Defence Dialogue is set up.
Background: Strategic Partnership since 2018; irritants are Khalistan extremism and the 2023 Nijjar issue; about 1.8 million Indo-Canadians; Canada is the top potash producer.
Para-diplomacy: foreign affairs is Item 10 of the Union List, so States can't override the Centre; examples of sensitivity are Tamil Nadu on Sri Lanka and West Bengal on Bangladesh.
Trincomalee oil tank farm: built by the British in the 1930s for naval fuel; India and Sri Lanka signed a 2022 pact for joint development.
Currency swaps: India-Japan bilateral swap; others are the SAARC CSA (2024-27), India-UAE and India-Sri Lanka.
Raisina Dialogue: ORF with the MEA in New Delhi since 2016; Raisina Science Diplomacy Initiative launched.

IOS SAGAR (second edition): naval personnel from 16 IONS countries sail on an Indian ship; GlobE Network steering meeting hosted by India; Panama Canal (about 82 km, since 1914) is at full capacity as Iran war pushes LNG traffic.
Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana aims to build 100 plug-and-play industrial parks of 100 to 1,000 acres, with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore for 2026-27 to 2031-32.
It is run by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry through DPIIT and the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation; a State or Central PSU is the sponsor.
A Special Purpose Vehicle of NICDIT and the State nodal agency develops each park, owns the assets and handles planning, building and upkeep.

Support is up to Rs 1 crore per acre (up to Rs 50 lakh per acre or 50% of infrastructure cost where private developers are involved); parks use underground utility corridors and align with PM GatiShakti.
India has signed DPI/India Stack MoUs with 24 countries (Feb 2026); UPI is live in the UAE, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius and Qatar; more than 25 nations use or study MOSIP.
India put DPI at the centre of the G20 development agenda in 2023.
Digital Public Goods are open-source software, standards, data, AI systems and content that build DPI; they are building blocks, not the infrastructure itself.
India's DPI grew from the JAM trinity (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) and links identity, finance and connectivity; it follows a co-creation model with the private sector.

FHI is NITI Aayog's index in its second annual edition. It uses CAG data for 2023-24 and ranks 18 major States and 10 North Eastern and Himalayan States separately; States hold nearly a third of general government debt.
Five pillars: Quality of Expenditure, Revenue Mobilisation, Fiscal Prudence, Debt Index and Debt Sustainability. Categories: Achiever, Front Runner, Performer, Aspirational.
Major States: Odisha tops the Achievers, Gujarat tops the Front Runners and Kerala is first among the Aspirational.
NE and Himalayan States have three groups with no Front Runner: Arunachal Pradesh tops the Achievers, Tripura the Performers and Nagaland the Aspirational.
India's first semiconductor assembly, test, marking and packaging (ATMP) facility is run by Micron and has begun India's first commercial chip production.
India meets only about 10% of its chip demand at home; the market was 52 billion dollars (2024-25) and is expected at 100-110 billion by 2030.

India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 was announced in Budget 2026-27; ISM includes a Design Linked Incentive scheme and a Display Fabs scheme; the Digital India RISC-V Programme produced SHAKTI and VIKRAM processors.
Taiwan accounts for over 60% of global chip manufacturing and nearly 90% of the most advanced chips.

Approved for 10 years (2026-27 to 2035-36) with Rs 28,840 crore: 100 airports from unserved airstrips over eight years (in 'Challenge Mode') and 200 helipads in hilly, remote, island and aspirational regions at Rs 15 crore each; VGF to airlines runs 10 years.
UDAN began on 21 October 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016: a Central Sector Scheme of Civil Aviation, run by the Airports Authority of India.
Record so far: 663 routes across 95 airports and Rs 4,593.28 crore of VGF; of 925 awarded routes, 327 were discontinued; airports rose from 74 (2014) to 159 (2024).
Versions: Krishi UDAN (perishables), UDAN 2.0 (helipads), 3.0 (tourism routes and seaplanes), 4.0 (hilly and island areas); UDAN Yatri Cafes at 17 airports.

Parliamentary Committee: DGCA has a 48.3% vacancy (843 against 1,630 posts), recurring defects in 377 of 754 audited aircraft, and there is no statutory passenger rights framework despite over 350 million passengers a year (suggested Passenger Rights Charter under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024).

Credit guarantee for microfinance institutions: corpus Rs 20,000 crore, managed by NCGTC under the Department of Financial Services. An NBFC-MFI keeps at least 75% of assets in collateral-free loans to households earning up to Rs 3 lakh a year; women are about 95% of borrowers.

Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs: 60% guarantee through NCGTC for loans up to Rs 100 crore, service-sector MSMEs now eligible, guarantee threshold cut to 60% of project cost (from 75%), cover valid for 10 years, special provisions for exporters.
Both are routed through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company, which gives lenders cover so they lend to borrowers without collateral.

topics.t: New GDP series, inflation target and core industries
p: New GDP series: base year 2022-23 replaces 2011-12 (chosen as the latest normal post-Covid year); double deflation in manufacturing and agriculture; GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data; Supply and Use Tables aligned; ASUSE and PLFS capture households and informal activity; gig and domestic work counted.

Inflation target 2026-31: the 4% target with a 2-6% band is retained (Urjit Patel committee idea; Section 45ZA of the RBI Act requires the Centre to set it every five years). Missing the band for three straight quarters is a failure. The Monetary Policy Committee has six members with the Governor as ex-officio chair.

Index of Core Industries: eight industries (coal, crude, gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, electricity) with about 40.27% weight in IIP; growth slowed to 2.3% in February from 4.7% in January; released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
ASUSE: the NSO's survey of unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises, feeding GDP estimates.

topics.t: FDI for land-border countries, energy and export news
p: FDI from land-border countries (Press Note 3, 2020 made it government-route only): non-controlling investors owning under 10% may now use the automatic route; proposals in electronics and capital goods are cleared in 60 days; majority control must remain with Indian residents.

Natural Gas and Petroleum Products Distribution Order 2026 (under the Essential Commodities Act 1955): four-tier priority allocation based on six months' gas use; non-priority industries such as power and petrochemicals are curtailed.

Strategic Petroleum Reserves: 5.33 million tonnes (about 9.5 days; IEA benchmark is 90); Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (2004); Phase-I at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur; Phase-II (2021, 6.5 MMT) at Chandikhol and Padur.
Gas share of India's energy mix: 6.2% (2025), target 15% by 2030. Biogas has 55-60% methane; GOBARdhan began in 2018.

Export Promotion Mission relief: ECGC (1957) reimburses up to 50% for eligible non-ECGC-insured MSME exporters hit by West Asia freight and war risks. RODTEP (2021) refunds unrebated taxes and replaced MEIS (a WTO issue).
National Shipping Board: statutory body of 1959 under the Merchant Shipping Act 1958; six members elected by Parliament (four from Lok Sabha, two from Rajya Sabha).
InvITs pool money from investors for infrastructure and are regulated by SEBI (InvIT Regulations 2014); NHAI's first public InvIT listed on BSE.
Bureau of Indian Standards: from the Indian Standards Institution (1947); BIS Act 2016 allows mandatory certification and hallmarking; over 23,300 standards; HQ New Delhi.
Coconut: India is the largest producer (nearly 30%); main States Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka; needs 1,000-2,500 mm rain and 20-32 degrees; Budget 2026-27 announced a Coconut Promotion Scheme.

MSMEs in defence: Union Budget 2026-27 gave the Defence Ministry a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore; iDEX and the Technology Development Fund support MSMEs; ideaForge makes UAVs, EyeROV and Sagar Defence build underwater and surface drones, Qnu Labs, QpiAI and Signalchip work on quantum-secure communication.
SIPRI arms transfers (2021-25): India is the second-largest importer with 8.2% of global imports (Ukraine is first); imports fell 4% from 2016-20; suppliers: Russia 40%, France 29%, Israel 15%.
Global Terrorism Index 2026 (Institute for Economics and Peace, Sydney): Pakistan scored highest; deaths down 28%, attacks down about 22%, about 70% of deaths in five countries, India 13th.

Kit in the news: six ALH Mk-III maritime helicopters from HAL for the Coast Guard; Vertical Launch Shtil air-defence missile (Rosoboronexport); Minuteman III is a US land-based ICBM; gravity bombs are unpowered free-fall bombs; Exercise Lamitiye (Seychelles) and Sea Dragon (US-led anti-submarine).

A draft under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 lets a Standing Authority on EIA take over for SEIAA for at most one year if it is non-functional (State bodies serve three years); a Standing Committee does the same for SEAC; if SEAC misses the 120-day appraisal limit the case moves up via the Parivesh portal.

Categories: Category A needs Centre clearance on an Expert Appraisal Committee's advice; Category B needs SEIAA clearance on SEAC's advice; B2 is exempt from EIA, as are solar and wind projects and hydro under 25 MW.
Judicial base: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum (polluter pays and precaution); Centre for Environmental Law v Union of India (2018) (public consultation).
India has not ratified the Espoo Convention (1991) on EIA in a transboundary context.

New 2035 targets: cut emissions intensity of GDP 47% from 2005 levels; 60% of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources; carbon sink of 3.5-4 billion tonnes CO2e. First NDC was 2015, updated 2022.
Non-fossil capacity share was 52.57% (Feb 2026) but gives under 30% of generation; coal is about 55% of electricity.

Tools: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (notified 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act 2001; refineries, cement, aluminium, textiles, pulp and paper), MISHTI for mangroves, the National Action Plan on Climate Change with State plans.
Challenges: transition investment of about 250 billion dollars a year till 2047 (NITI Aayog), battery storage cost and dependence on imported critical minerals like lithium.

The Kunming-Montreal framework (COP15, 2022; replaced Aichi targets; non-binding) has 23 targets for 2030 including 30 by 30; at least 200 billion dollars a year; developed countries to give 20 billion a year by 2025 and 30 billion by 2030; cut harmful subsidies by 500 billion; halve invasive species and pesticide risks; financed through the GEF-managed GBFF (20% for indigenous peoples).

India's report (Article 26 of CBD, tracks 23 NBSAP 2024-30 targets): forest and tree cover 25.17% (recorded forest 23.59%); 24.1 million ha under restoration against a 26 million ha Bonn pledge; 98 Ramsar sites (1st in Asia, 3rd globally); 3,682 tigers, 718 snow leopards, 6,327 river dolphins, 22,446 elephants, 891 Asiatic lions.
Protected areas 5.71% of land: 58 tiger reserves, 18 biosphere reserves, 574 sanctuaries, 106 national parks, 390 community and 145 conservation reserves; 29.77% of land is degraded.

Nagoya Protocol (adopted 2010, in force 2014; prior informed consent, mutually agreed terms): India's first national report shows 12,830 ABS approvals, 3,556 compliance certificates (about 60% of the world), over 2.76 lakh BMCs and Rs 216.31 crore mobilised (Rs 139.69 crore distributed).

topics.t: International Solar Alliance and glacier melt
p: ISA marked 10 years on 11 March 2026; the PM called it an 'alternative OPEC'; it pools demand to help LDCs and small island States and supports SDG 7 and 13.
A ISRO study traced the Srikanta glacier event to collapse of an exposed ice patch in the nivation zone, not a cloudburst or GLOF.

Himalayan glacier loss has doubled since 2000; Karakoram stayed relatively stable (about 2% loss); Ganga and Brahmaputra basins lost 21% and 16% of glacier area; small glaciers under 0.5 sq km shrink fastest; 12% of glacier area and 9% of ice reserves were lost between 1990 and 2020.
NDMA's GLOF programme: Phase 1 (2023-26) for Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal, J&K and Ladakh; Jal Shakti and CWC are the nodal bodies; examples are Chamoli 2021, Sikkim 2023, Dharali 2025.

Small Hydro Development Scheme: Rs 2,584.60 crore for about 1,500 MW in 2026-27 to 2030-31 (MNRE); small hydro is up to 25 MW (micro up to 100 kW, mini 101 kW to 2 MW, small 2-25 MW); potential 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites.
CMS interim report: 49% of listed migratory species are declining and 24% are threatened. UN World Water Development Report 2026 ('Water and Gender'): 2.1 billion lack safely managed drinking water.

SDG Bulletin: renewables share of installed capacity rose from 16.02% to 22.13% (2015-16 to 2024-25); door-to-door waste collection from 43% to 97.7%. WMO: Earth's energy imbalance at a 65-year peak; 2025 was about 1.43 degrees above 1850-1900; 2015-2025 are the 11 hottest years.

NH Green Cover Index (NHAI with NRSC): covers about 30,000 km of highways. National Productivity Council is the Environment Audit designated agency (Environment Audit Rules 2025) under DPIIT. BEE marked 25 years.

M.C. Mehta case: absolute liability; Godavarman (1995) widened 'forest'; S.P. Muthuraman (2025) held post-facto environmental clearance illegal. OTEC plant planned at Kavaratti (needs about 20 degrees difference, between 30 N and S). Dark oxygen was found at about 4,000 m depth. Shipki La (Sutlej enters India there) reopens for trade. Rossby waves can trap heat; wet-bulb above 31.5 degrees is harmful.

Supreme Court allowed, for the first time, withdrawal of life support for a man in a vegetative state for 13 years; it treats Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration as medical treatment that may be withdrawn if futile, and waived the usual 30-day wait as parents and boards agreed.

Active euthanasia is illegal. Gian Kaur (1996): right to life does not include a right to die. Common Cause (2018): passive euthanasia and living wills allowed with strict safeguards; 2023 guidelines eased the process with medical boards and judicial officers.
A living will is an advance instruction on medical treatment for when a person becomes incompetent.

Amends the 2019 Act: the District Magistrate certifies identity after a designated medical board's recommendation; Section 4(2) (self-determination) is omitted and self-perceived identities are excluded; critics say trans-men and non-binary people are excluded.
National Council for Transgender Persons gets rotational State/UT representation (one each from North, South, East, West, North-East) at Director rank.
New offences: kidnapping or grievous hurt to force a person into a transgender identity; forcing someone to present as transgender for begging or bonded labour.
Census 2011: 4.8 lakh transgender persons, literacy 56.1% (national 74.04%); the Yogyakarta Principles favour self-identification; about 96% faced employment discrimination (NHRC 2018).

CARA is a statutory body under the Women and Child Development Ministry (set up 1990, statutory under the JJ Act 2015) and the Central Authority for inter-country adoption under the Hague Convention (India ratified 2003); SARAs, CWCs and DCPUs work below it.
Laws: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956 (Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs; no CARA registration needed), Guardians and Wards Act 1890 (Muslims, Christians), JJ Act 2015 (open to all).
CARINGS is CARA's portal built by NIC and merged with Mission Vatsalya; surrendered children get a two-month reconsideration period; Section 74 JJ Act bars disclosing identities.
Supreme Court struck down Section 60(4) of the Social Security Code 2020 (maternity benefit only if the adopted child was under 3 months), citing Article 21 autonomy; biological mothers get 26 weeks.
AI in education: NEP 2020 acknowledges AI, big data and ML; SOAR builds AI skills for classes 6-12 and educators; SWAYAM offers free AI courses from IITs and IISc; UGC's 2022 curriculum adds AI.
Impact4Nutrition: NITI Aayog and UNICEF India signed a Statement of Intent to link businesses with POSHAN 2.0 in aspirational districts; the ACE Card means Assets, CSR and Employees engagement.
Capacity rose from about 375 MW (2020) to about 1,500 MW (2025); over 70% sits in Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad; data centres above 5 MW IT load got infrastructure status in 2022.
Budget 2026-27: tax holiday till 2047 for eligible foreign cloud providers serving from India; 15% safe harbour where an Indian data centre is a related entity of a foreign company.

Concerns: a 100 MW hyperscale facility can use up to 2 million litres of water a day; IEA expects data centre power demand to nearly double by 2030; immersion and direct-to-chip cooling save water and power.

NavIC is ISRO's independent regional navigation system with a service area about 1,500 km beyond India; it needs at least 4 satellites with working atomic clocks, but the last clock on IRNSS-1F stopped, leaving three (1B, 1I and NVS-01) for PNT, with 6 of 11 satellites hit by clock failures.
IRNSS-1A (2013) was the first; NVS-01 (GSLV-F12, 2023) carried the first indigenous atomic clock; NVS-02 missed its orbit; the NVS series adds L1 to the L5 and S bands.
Services: Standard Positioning (civil, better than 20 m position and 40 ns timing; interoperable with GPS, Glonass, Galileo, BeiDou) and an encrypted Restricted Service.
Why it matters: it cuts reliance on US-owned GPS (GPS was denied in Kargil); about 8,700 trains carry NavIC.

The new particle (made of two charm quarks and one down quark) is the 80th particle discovered at the LHC; its mass is about four times a proton's because charm quarks replace up quarks, and it helps study the strong force.

Quarks come in six flavours (up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom). Baryons (protons, neutrons) have three quarks; mesons (pions, kaons) have two. The strong force is about 100 times stronger than electromagnetism but very short range.
LHC: 27 km ring of superconducting magnets about 100 m underground at CERN (founded 1954, Franco-Swiss border near Geneva; India is an associate member). It found the Higgs boson in 2012.

The Food Safety and Standards (Fortification of Food) Regulations 2018 set standards for fortifying rice, wheat flour, edible oil, milk and salt; Fortified Rice Kernels are blended with regular rice at 1:100.

Types: bio-fortification (nutrients built in while crops grow, e.g. orange sweet potato), industrial fortification (added in processing, e.g. iodine in salt) and home fortification (sprinkles or sachets).
A scheme was paused after an IIT Kharagpur study questioned nutrient stability; concerns include lower bioavailability and shelf-life loss.
Launched 28 February 2026 for 14-year-old girls: free, single dose of Gardasil-4 given into muscle, parental consent mandatory, 90-day intensive run at government facilities.
HPV types 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers worldwide and over 80% in India. Gardasil-4 covers types 6, 11, 16, 18; Cervavac is the indigenous quadrivalent vaccine from Serum Institute.

WHO 90-70-90 goals: 90% of girls vaccinated by 15, 70% of women screened at 35 and 45, 90% of cases treated. U-WIN registers beneficiaries; eVIN tracks stock; Gavi (2000, public-private) supplies doses.
Trust history: a 2011 parliamentary committee found no conclusive link between the 2009 PATH project and the girls' deaths.

topics.t: Science and technology news in brief (March)
p: IndiaAI Mission used only 32% of its 2025-26 revised estimate (as of Dec 2025) and its 2026-27 budget was halved; funding is mostly to IITs and national labs.

Brain co-processors are AI-powered two-way neural interfaces, aimed at restoring reach and grasp after stroke. Digital Twin: V.O. Chidambaranar (Thoothukudi) is India's first port with it (virtual copy fed by IoT, GPS, LiDAR, drones, CCTV).
KAVACH, from RDSO, prevents head-on, rear-end and side collisions and repeats signals in fog; V2X lets vehicles talk to other vehicles, pedestrians and roadside units (spectrum being allocated).

GARBH-INi (DBT; Gurugram, since 2015) is one of South Asia's largest pregnancy cohorts, building AI tools for preterm birth. Rare earth permanent magnet scheme: 6,000 MTPA, five bidders up to 1,200 MTPA each, Rs 750 crore capital subsidy and Rs 6,450 crore sales incentive.

World Obesity Atlas 2026: school-age obesity rose from 4% (1975) to nearly 20% (2022); India is second for overweight children (about 41 million). GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic, Wegovy) mimic a hormone that controls sugar and appetite; CDSCO banned their advertising. White fat stores energy; brown fat burns it as heat.

Antiprotons (same mass as a proton, negative charge) were moved by road at CERN for the first time. MeerKAT found the brightest, most distant megamaser. CSIR-NCL developed DME production; DME can be blended with LPG up to 20%.

Led by Dr B.R. Ambedkar on 20 March 1927 to secure Dalits' right to draw water from the Chawdar Tank, organised by the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924); 20 March is Social Empowerment Day and the centenary runs through 2026-27.

Background: in 1923 the Bombay Legislative Council opened state-funded water places to untouchables; the Mahad municipality did so in 1924 but nothing changed. A lawsuit claiming the tank was private stopped the second satyagraha; on 17 March 1937 the Bombay High Court declared it public.

Comparisons: Satyashodhak Samaj (Phule, 1873), Self-Respect Movement (Periyar, 1925), Harijan Sevak Sangh (Gandhi, 1932). It pushed Congress to reconstitute its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
It reflects Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) and Article 15 (no discrimination in access to wells and tanks).

topics.t: Gyan Bharatam manuscript survey and Sahitya Akademi
p: Gyan Bharatam: a Central Sector scheme of the Ministry of Culture, Rs 491.66 crore for 2025-2031, to digitise and catalogue over 1 crore manuscripts using AI, OCR and blockchain; builds on the National Mission for Manuscripts and will create a geo-tagged inventory and a Manuscript Presence Map.
Article 51A(f) makes it a duty to value and preserve the composite culture; the Bakhshali Manuscript has early discussion of zero; the Rigveda is recognised by UNESCO.
Sahitya Akademi: national academy of letters, an autonomous body; formally set up 1952, inaugurated 12 March 1954; 2025 awards in 24 languages (Navtej Sarna for the English novel Crimson Spring).

topics.t: National security, AI and ethics; Happiness
p: Utilitarianism backs AI in defence for the greatest security for the majority; a deontological view says some lines must not be crossed whatever the gain; black-box systems make accountability and humanitarian-law compliance hard. India has a Defence AI Council and Project Agency.
World Happiness Report 2026 (Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre, Gallup, UN SDSN; Cantril Ladder 0-10): Finland first for the ninth year; India up from 118th to 116th; Nepal 99th; Pakistan 104th.
Ideas: Taittiriya Upanishad (Brahman as Sat-Chit-Ananda), Aristotle's Eudaimonia, Bhutan's Gross National Happiness, Delhi Happiness Curriculum (2018; nearly 8 lakh students), UNESCO 'Happy Schools'.
Cabinet extended the Mission till December 2028. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Jal Shakti (2019) aiming at a functional household tap with 55 litres per person per day.
Tap water coverage rose from 3.23 crore homes (16.7%) in 2019 to 15.83 crore (about 81.8%) in 2026.

Community role: Paani Samitis run schemes with at least 50% women; Village Action Plans cover sources, grey water reuse and upkeep; at least five women per village are trained to test water; Nal Jal Mitras repair schemes.
2024 functionality assessment: 98.1% of households in surveyed villages had taps, 84% got water on schedule, 80% got at least 55 LPCD and 76% of connections were functional.
